title: Website redesign for small businesses
description: Refresh an outdated business website with Picshaw. Mobile-first design, clear enquiry paths and SEO foundations, with a $1,000 refresh option.
intro: Keep what works. Fix what gets in the way. Picshaw helps local businesses turn an outdated website into a clearer, more useful place to call, enquire or request a quote.

sections.title: A refresh or a rebuild? Start with the actual problem.
paragraphs: A refresh is worth considering when your services and existing content are still right, but the design, mobile experience or route to an enquiry needs attention. A rebuild may be more appropriate when you need a different structure, more service pages or a new integration.

For example, a contractor with accurate service information but a hard-to-find phone number has a different brief from a company adding several new services. We review your existing site before recommending the scope. This is a scoping example, not a client result.

sections.title: What the website refresh focuses on
paragraphs: The published Website Refresh package is $1,000. The starting point is the existing offer: visual redesign, mobile-first layout, click-to-call and quote forms, SEO structure, a clear contact experience and basic analytics setup. The written scope confirms the pages and changes before work begins.
bullets: Make the main service and next step obvious on mobile and desktop.
Restructure existing content so visitors can find services, location and contact details.
Set page titles, headings and descriptions that reflect the real business.
Test the enquiry path rather than treating the form's appearance as proof that it works.

sections.title: Do not lose the useful parts of the old site
paragraphs: Before changing an existing website, we identify important URLs and available search data. Where addresses need to change, relevant redirects and updated internal links belong in the launch scope. We do not assume every old page should be redirected to the homepage.

A redesign is not a promise that rankings will stay unchanged. Search systems need to process changes, and the migration plan depends on the current site. Tell us about domain, hosting, booking or email dependencies before the launch is scheduled.

sources.label: Google: site moves with URL changes

sections.title: When the Growth Site is the better fit
paragraphs: Picshaw's Growth Site starts at $2,500 and is the published option for a 5–10 page site. Projects that need more pages, new integrations or a different content structure need a confirmed quote rather than an assumption that everything fits the refresh.

Domain renewals, hosting arrangements, third-party subscriptions, new photography and ongoing content work should be clarified in the proposal. The refresh price is not a promise of unlimited work or lifetime third-party services. You receive a handoff; the ownership and account-transfer details are agreed for your project.

questions.question: Can you work with my existing website?
questions.answer: Yes. Send its address with the review request. The recommendation depends on its structure, content and any platform or integration constraints.

questions.question: Does a redesign guarantee more leads?
questions.answer: No. The work improves the website and enquiry path; traffic quality, your offer, competition and follow-up also affect the outcome. We measure enquiries rather than promising a percentage increase.

questions.question: Is ongoing SEO included forever?
questions.answer: No. Technical foundations and an ongoing acquisition programme are different scopes. Picshaw's published Monthly Partner option starts at $500 per month; confirm the deliverables in your proposal.

title: AI-search optimization for local businesses
description: Make your business website easier to discover and understand in search. Picshaw audits crawlability, useful content, evidence and AI-search eligibility.
intro: Give search systems useful, accessible information about your business. Picshaw's approach to answer engine optimization starts with a website people can trust—not a promise to make an AI assistant recommend you.

sections.title: What AEO work actually involves
paragraphs: Answer engine optimization describes work intended to improve visibility in AI-powered search experiences. For Picshaw, that means checking access, explaining your services clearly, supporting claims with evidence and measuring relevant visits and enquiries.
Google says its generative search features build on its core search systems. We therefore treat AI-search work as an extension of useful content and sound SEO, not a replacement for them.

sources.label: Google: optimizing for generative AI search

sections.title: First, check whether public pages can be read
paragraphs: The audit covers robots rules, indexing directives, canonical URLs, sitemaps, readable page content and crawlable links. Hosting-level restrictions are checked separately: an open robots file does not override a firewall or a login.
OpenAI documents OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT search and GPTBot for potential training use. These are separate controls. We do not change a business's training preference merely to enable search access.

links.label: Read the ChatGPT search eligibility guide

sections.title: Then, give people a reason to choose your business
paragraphs: We look for unanswered buying questions: what you do, who you serve, where you work, what happens next and what your prices include. Those questions belong on useful service pages, supported by real examples and a named business.

Concept designs must be labelled as concepts. Results need a source and a timeframe. We will not manufacture client reviews, awards, rankings or third-party endorsements to make the site look established.
bullets: Specific service explanations and accurate business information.
Practical guides that connect to a relevant next step.
First-hand examples where available, with concept work clearly distinguished.
Structured data that matches the content visitors can actually read.

sections.title: Measure visibility separately from business outcomes
paragraphs: We use the search and analytics data available for your accounts. Identifiable AI referrals, landing-page visits and completed enquiries are different measures; none should be presented as the other.

No provider can guarantee that ChatGPT or Google will cite a particular page. A useful first engagement is a scoped audit and implementation plan. Ongoing content and promotion are agreed separately, after the basics and measurement are in place.

questions.question: Can you guarantee a ChatGPT recommendation?
questions.answer: No. We can improve the information and access you control, but the search platform decides what appears for a particular request.

questions.question: Is an llms.txt file the main solution?
questions.answer: No. Google explicitly says it does not use llms.txt to improve visibility. We prioritise useful pages, accurate information, real evidence and ordinary search foundations.

questions.question: How is the work priced?
questions.answer: Send your website for a review. We confirm the audit, technical fixes and content scope before quoting. The $1,000 website refresh is not an unlimited ongoing AEO package.

title: Local SEO for small service businesses
description: Build a clearer local search presence with Picshaw: technical checks, service content, genuine business information and enquiry-focused measurement.
intro: Help nearby customers understand what you offer and how to contact you. Start with an honest diagnosis of the website, then invest in the pages and improvements that fit your business.

sections.title: Not indexed, or just not ranking? They are different problems.
paragraphs: A page can be accessible and indexed without attracting enquiries. Before prescribing more posts, we inspect important URLs and review the available Search Console data. That separates an access problem from a content, relevance or demand problem.

An early report should state what was checked, what the data actually says and where access is still missing. A low-traffic website does not need an invented forecast; it needs a clear baseline and an ordered set of changes.

links.label: Diagnose a site that is not appearing in Google

sections.title: Build pages around real services—not every keyword variation
paragraphs: We organise the site around distinct services and useful customer questions. A service-area page should add meaningful information about where and how the business operates, not just replace the city name in a template.

The scope can include titles, descriptions, headings, internal links, canonical URLs and a sitemap. Content work then explains the business clearly and gives visitors an appropriate route to call or request a quote.

sections.title: Keep business information genuine and consistent
paragraphs: Business profiles and website details should agree about the name, contact information and services. Reviews should come from real customers and reflect their own experience.

Google Business Profile work is appropriate only for an eligible business. Qualifying in-person customer contact matters; an online-only business should not create a fictitious office to obtain a local listing. We check eligibility before adding profile work to the scope.

sections.title: Separate launch foundations from ongoing work
paragraphs: Picshaw's website packages include SEO foundations. Ongoing local SEO may require new content, improvements to existing pages, profile maintenance and review of results. The published Monthly Partner option starts at $500 per month; the actual work is confirmed in a proposal.

We recommend judging the programme by relevant search visits, completed enquiries and qualified conversations. Ranking screenshots and traffic totals are supporting information, not proof of new customers.

questions.question: Can you promise the first position in my city?
questions.answer: No. Rankings depend on the query, competition and the search system. We agree the work and measurement, not a guaranteed position.

questions.question: Should I create a page for every neighbourhood?
questions.answer: Only where there is genuinely useful, distinct information. We do not recommend a large set of near-identical location pages just to capture keyword variations.

questions.question: Do I need to replace my whole website?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. The review may identify fixes that can be made on your current site. A redesign should solve a real problem, not be the default recommendation.

title: Web design for contractors and home-service businesses
description: Contractor websites with clear services, mobile-friendly contact options and useful quote forms. Picshaw serves local businesses from Los Angeles.
intro: Show people what you do, where you work and how to request an estimate. Picshaw designs websites around the practical questions a homeowner asks before getting in touch.

sections.title: Make the first screen earn its place
paragraphs: Our starting point is straightforward: name the trade, explain the service area and make the next step obvious. A homeowner with a leaking pipe should not have to interpret a vague slogan before finding out whether you can help.

For a plumbing business, an illustrative first screen might identify the plumbing services offered, give the actual coverage area and provide a tap-to-call option plus an estimate request. Emergency availability should appear only when the business genuinely provides it. This is a design example, not a measured client outcome.

sections.title: Ask for enough information—not everything
paragraphs: A useful enquiry form can ask for contact details, the type of job and the location information needed to decide whether it is in scope. Photos or scheduling integrations may help some businesses, but those features should be scoped rather than promised by default.
Before launch, test where messages arrive, how errors are explained and what the customer sees after submission. Do not display a successful confirmation when no enquiry has been delivered.
bullets: Clear service navigation on a small screen.
A working phone link using the business's real number.
An estimate request with explicit required fields.

sections.title: Use proof you can stand behind
paragraphs: Use your actual project photographs with permission, describe the work accurately and include credentials only when they are current and applicable. Testimonials should be genuine and authorised.

Picshaw's homepage includes labelled design concepts to demonstrate design direction. They are not customer case studies or evidence of increased bookings. A project case study should be added only when the client, work and any reported outcomes are verified.

sections.title: Choose the scope around the business
paragraphs: The $1,000 Website Refresh may suit an established site whose existing content needs a stronger presentation and enquiry path. A Growth Site from $2,500 is the published option for a 5–10 page website with a broader service structure.

Roofers, landscapers, plumbers and other trades have different information needs. We review the existing website and agree which pages and functionality are needed; there is no assumption that every trade needs the same template.

questions.question: Can I keep my current domain?
questions.answer: Often yes. We review the existing domain, hosting and email arrangements before agreeing a migration so the website change does not assume those services can be moved together.

questions.question: Can you add online booking or job-management software?
questions.answer: We can assess the integration you need. Compatibility, subscription costs and implementation effort must be confirmed in the scope; they are not automatically included in the refresh.

questions.question: What should I send for a review?
questions.answer: Your current website address, your main services and the areas you actually cover. Explain whether your priority is calls, estimate requests or a different action.
